attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in his own voice. Not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense statement about September 2023. The normalised version drops 'really' and 'whatsoever' but keeps the core: there was no societal plan to mitigate long-term AI risks. It is somewhat rhetorical but still checkable.

contract.note: The plain reading (an adopted public plan linking threat assessment to response, with named actors) is ordinary and fair. Company policies, proposals, and research do not count, which matches the post. Scope and how developed a plan must be are left open by the speaker, so the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: UK Taskforce progress report, 7 Sep 2023. Describes public research and evaluation partnerships, i.e. preparation, but no response plan. Does not show whether any plan existed elsewhere.

White House fact sheet, 12 Sep 2023. Voluntary company commitments are called a 'bridge' to government action, and the executive order was still being drafted. Consistent with the claim but not a full account of what existed. Government self-description.

UK summit announcement, 4 Sep 2023. Practical next steps and a longer-term roadmap were still to be agreed, but it cites existing initiatives (OECD, G7, etc.) without saying what they contain. Cannot establish absence.

reviews.rationale: All three items point to preparation rather than an adopted plan: research teams, voluntary commitments, and a summit still to agree a roadmap. That fits Marcus's claim. But the contract says showing absence needs more than not finding a plan, and the packet admits it is not a full survey (OECD, G7, UN work is unexamined). Nothing contradicts the claim, but the evidence does not settle it either way.
